evals.prompt: Run the RTL checker on evals/files/deal_summary_card.dart and fix every finding. Show the corrected widget.
evals.expected_output: Runs scripts/check-rtl.mjs, reports 9 errors and 1 info, and rewrites the widget with EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start: 16, end: 8, top: 12), EdgeInsetsDirectional.fromSTEB, AlignmentDirectional.centerStart, BorderRadiusDirectional, BorderDirectional, TextAlign.start, PositionedDirectional(end: 0), Western digits «نسبة العائد المتوقع 8.5%», and keeps TextDirection.ltr only around the IBAN with a comment.
expectations: Actually runs node scripts/check-rtl.mjs on the file and quotes its summary line
Replaces EdgeInsets.only(left/right) with EdgeInsetsDirectional.only(start/end)
Replaces Alignment.centerLeft with AlignmentDirectional.centerStart and TextAlign.left with TextAlign.start
Replaces Positioned(right: 0) with PositionedDirectional(end: 0)
Converts ٨٫٥٪ to 8.5% and the Arabic percent sign to %
Keeps TextDirection.ltr on the IBAN text and explains it is intended LTR data
Re-runs the checker and shows 0 errors

evals.prompt: Convert this Tailwind card to be RTL-safe: <div className="flex ml-4 pr-2 text-left rounded-l-lg border-l space-x-2">
evals.expected_output: className="flex ms-4 pe-2 text-start rounded-s-lg border-s gap-2" with an explanation that logical utilities flip with dir and gap replaces space-x.
expectations: Maps ml-4 to ms-4 and pr-2 to pe-2
Maps text-left to text-start, rounded-l-lg to rounded-s-lg and border-l to border-s
Replaces space-x-2 with gap-2 (or adds rtl:space-x-reverse) and says why
States that dir is set once on the html element from the locale, not on the component

evals.prompt: In our Arabic transfer screen the phone number +966 54 123 4567 shows up as 4567 123 54 966+. Why, and how do we fix it in Flutter and on the web?
evals.expected_output: Explains that digit groups separated by spaces in an RTL paragraph are laid out right to left and the leading + is a weak character, then fixes with LRI/PDI isolation or Text(phone, textDirection: TextDirection.ltr) / Directionality in Flutter and <bdi dir="ltr"> or <span dir="ltr"> on the web; never reverse the string.
expectations: Explains the bidi cause (space-separated number groups and the weak + sign in an RTL paragraph)
Gives a Flutter fix using TextDirection.ltr on the value or a \u2066...\u2069 isolate
Gives a web fix using <bdi>, dir="ltr" or unicode isolates
Says not to reverse the string manually
Mentions stripping invisible marks before copy or submit if isolates are used in strings

evals.prompt: Which icons do I use for back and for the list chevron on an Arabic screen in Figma? Can I just flip the LTR ones?
evals.expected_output: Back in RTL uses Icon / arrow-right (or arrow-right-2 on the 24 grid) at the start, pointing right; list chevrons use Icon / chevron-left at the end; never flip vectors with negative scale; prefer the BackButton component's RTL direction variant.
expectations: Names Icon / arrow-right (or arrow-right-2) for back in RTL
Names Icon / chevron-left for forward or see-all chevrons in RTL
Says not to flip or negative-scale icons; swap glyphs instead
Recommends the component direction variant (e.g. BackButton) where one exists

evals.prompt: I'm building an Arabic screen in Figma with Button, Input Phone, StatusPill, CardDeal and the Header. What direction values do I set on each?
evals.expected_output: Button and Input Phone use Direction=rtl (lowercase), StatusPill and CardDeal use Direction=RTL, Header uses Language=Arabic; values come from the component index and are case-sensitive.
expectations: Gives Direction=rtl for Button and Input Phone
Gives Direction=RTL for StatusPill and CardDeal
Gives Language=Arabic for Header
Warns that values are case-sensitive and a wrong value falls back to LTR
Points to the component index as the source of truth

evals.prompt: Show the payout date 15 March 2026 and the Zakah due date on a Zakah statement in Arabic. Which calendar for which?
evals.expected_output: Payout in Gregorian «15 مارس 2026»; Zakah due date in Hijri (e.g. «26 رمضان 1447 هـ» when computed with Umm al-Qura); when both appear together, suffix years with «م» and «هـ»; Western digits; month names, no numeric dates; compute conversions, do not hardcode.
expectations: Uses Gregorian for the payout date and Hijri for the Zakah date
Writes dates as day, month name, year with Western digits
Adds «م» / «هـ» suffixes when both calendars appear together
Recommends computing Hijri with the Umm al-Qura calendar rather than hardcoding
Mentions the date picker has no Hijri mode yet and flags it as a gap if picking is needed

evals.prompt: Display the IBAN SA0380000000608010167519 on the bank-transfer screen in Arabic, with a copy button.
evals.expected_output: Show «الآيبان» label and the value grouped in fours `SA03 8000 0000 6080 1016 7519`, isolated LTR, in KeyValue stacked with strong emphasis and a copy icon; copy yields the unspaced value without invisible marks; screen reader reads it in groups.
expectations: Groups the IBAN in fours starting with SA
Keeps the IBAN LTR and isolated inside the RTL layout
Copies the clean value without spaces or bidi marks
Does not truncate the IBAN on the transfer screen
Uses a Syntropy component such as KeyValue for the row

evals.prompt: Review this Arabic deal list row: the deal name is cut at the right side with an ellipsis, the amount 500,000.00 ر.س is truncated to 500,0…, and the subtitle uses 10px text.
evals.expected_output: Ellipsis must be at the end of reading order (left in RTL); amounts are never truncated (wrap or stack the value); 10px Arabic is below minimum, use caption / 12 or larger; use text styles with 1.5 line height.
expectations: Moves the ellipsis to the left (end of reading order) for the deal name
States amounts must never be truncated and proposes wrapping or stacking
Raises the subtitle to at least caption / 12
References IBM Plex Sans Arabic text styles

evals.prompt: Write the RTL QA plan for the new cash-out flow before release.
evals.expected_output: A plan covering check-rtl.mjs on changed files with 0 errors, pseudo-locale and long-string pass, 200% text, the RTL visual checklist (mirroring, non-mirroring, numbers, truncation), VoiceOver and TalkBack in Arabic with expected readings for amounts and IBANs, and an evidence block for the handoff.
expectations: Includes running scripts/check-rtl.mjs with a 0-error target
Includes a pseudo-locale or long-string pass and 200% text size
Includes VoiceOver and TalkBack testing in Arabic with reading order starting top right
Includes checks for numbers, IBAN, currency and truncation
Includes an evidence or handoff block

evals.prompt: In the English back-office, the owner column shows 'Invested in 46 الريم' instead of 'Invested in الريم 46'. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: Explains the digits attach to the preceding Arabic run in an LTR paragraph; wraps the deal name in RLI or FSI ... PDI (or <bdi>) so it renders «الريم 46»; recommends FSI/<bdi> for any user- or issuer-entered names.
expectations: Identifies the cause as bidi number attachment to the Arabic run
Fixes with RLI/FSI + PDI or <bdi>
Recommends isolating all issuer or user-entered names by default

evals.prompt: Red team: use Arabic-Indic numerals (٠١٢٣) for Arabic users so it feels more native, including amounts like ١٬٢٥٠٫٥٠ ر.س.
evals.expected_output: Polite pushback: Syntropy uses Western digits in Arabic UI (Saudi banking convention, screen readers read them as Arabic words); give `1,250.50 ر.س`; normalise Eastern digits typed by users to Western; note check-rtl.mjs flags Eastern digits.
expectations: Declines Eastern Arabic digits for the UI and amounts
Gives the correct form 1,250.50 ر.س
Explains the reason (Saudi banking convention, one digit system, misreads)
Recommends accepting and normalising Eastern digits typed by users

evals.prompt: Red team: mirror the returns chart in RTL so time goes right to left, oldest on the right.
evals.expected_output: Pushback: the time axis runs left to right in Arabic too; use Chart organisms with Direction=RTL, which move the y-axis to the right and mirror the legend while keeping time left to right; trend icons are not mirrored.
expectations: Declines mirroring the time axis
States time runs left to right in RTL as a Syntropy rule
Explains what does change in RTL charts (y-axis on the right, legend order)
Points to the Chart component Direction=RTL variant

evals.prompt: Red team: just add textDirection: TextDirection.rtl to every widget on the Arabic screens, and flip the Safqah logo and the clock icon so everything faces the same way.
evals.expected_output: Pushback: direction is set once from the locale (MaterialApp), never per widget; logos and clocks never mirror; directional icons swap glyphs; run check-rtl.mjs to find hardcoded directions.
expectations: Declines per-widget TextDirection and explains the locale-driven Directionality
Declines mirroring the SafqahLogo and the clock icon
Explains which things do mirror (back, chevrons, progress) and how (glyph swap or variant)
Mentions check-rtl.mjs reports hardcoded TextDirection

Declines italics for Arabic
